references.name: Adam Smith
references.connection:
Foundational text: invisible hand, division of labor,
    comparative advantage, demolition of mercantilism

references.name: Lionel Robbins
references.connection:
Provided the classic definition of economics as the study of
    scarce resources with alternative uses

references.name: Friedrich Hayek
references.desc: The Use of Knowledge in Society (1945)
references.connection:
Price system as information-processing mechanism; knowledge
    problem of central planning

references.name: Milton Friedman
references.desc: Monetarist economics; A Monetary History of the U.S.
references.connection:
Great Depression caused by Fed's money supply contraction;
    market solutions superior to government intervention

references.name: John Maynard Keynes
references.connection:
Fiscal policy and aggregate demand management; dominant
    framework from 1940s to 1970s, challenged by stagflation

references.name: David Ricardo
references.connection:
Theory of comparative advantage: both countries gain from
    trade even when one is better at everything

references.name: Thomas Malthus
references.desc: An Essay on the Principle of Population (1798)
references.connection:
Population grows geometrically, food arithmetically — prediction
    falsified by technological change

references.name: Carl Menger
references.connection:
Marginal utility theory, independently developed; resolved
    the water-diamonds paradox

references.name: W. Stanley Jevons
references.desc: The Theory of Political Economy (1871, England)
references.connection:
Marginal utility theory, independently developed; added
    mathematical/graphical formulation

references.name: Alfred Marshall
references.connection:
Supply and demand synthesis; elasticity; consumer surplus;
    dominant textbook for decades

references.name: Karl Marx
references.connection:
Labor theory of value taken to extreme; exploitation theory;
    predictions tested and refuted at enormous scale

references.name: Peter Bauer
references.connection:
Critique of foreign aid; distinction between economic equality
    and poverty alleviation

references.name: George Stigler
references.connection:
Opening epigraph on the universal value of economic knowledge
    regardless of political position

references.name: William Easterly
references.connection:
On the wonder of markets reconciling the choices of myriad
    individuals without central direction

references.name: Augustin Cournot
references.connection:
Early mathematical economics; work largely unknown until
    rediscovered generations later — a cautionary tale about
    how ideas can be lost

connections.title: The Man Who Solved the Market
connections.author: Gregory Zuckerman
